_note: Millennium Lab: one bot per department. Lab jobs run in parallel in lab_pool.py (pool.workers at once, OpenCode and Copilot CLI), not in the one-at-a-time Cairn autopilot. slots = jobs a department may have open at once; every_hours = minimum gap between its jobs; paused = true stops it. Prize-winnable work (Squares, Erdos) gets the most slots.

departments.name: Murmuration Desk
departments.role: Elliptic-curve statistics: local densities, trace formula, Sawin-Sutherland comparison
departments.brief: Continue the BSD thread. Read bsd_project/FINDINGS.md and roadmap.json BSD first. Next open items: derive a_c and c_c as explicit local densities (q-adic Hurwitz averages); compare the measured a2-weighted scale with Sawin-Sutherland arXiv:2504.12295; extend checks to new conductor ranges. Add the dated result line to bsd_project/FINDINGS.md under '## Automated runs'.

departments.name: Zeta Desk
departments.role: Zero statistics: finite-height corrections, BBLM amplitude, k-fit
departments.brief: Continue the RH thread. Read rh_project/FINDINGS.md and roadmap.json RH first. Next open items: compare the 9-height BBLM amplitudes with the Bogomolny et al. 2006 second-order term; widen the exploratory k ~ 1.1 fit; test other statistics (number variance, nearest-neighbour tails) on the stored zeros. Add the dated result line to rh_project/FINDINGS.md under '## Automated runs'.

departments.name: Erdos Bench
departments.role: One open Erdos prize problem per job: literature + forum check, computation, honest status
departments.brief: Work the Erdos prize problem named below. Read its erdosproblems.com page, comments and cited papers first (many have recent partial results). Write prize_work/<id>.md: exact statement, prize, what is known (with references), and one computation you ran (script in prize_work/<id>/ with a gate reproducing a known value, e.g. a published small case). If you find something that looks new, set status needs_review with one line why; never post on the forum or claim a prize. Check erdosproblems.com for the current status first (many are solved or have partial results). Any claimed proof must come with a Lean 4 statement (and proof if the toolchain is installed) in prize_work/<id>/lean/; without it the result stays needs_review.

departments.name: Bounty Hunters
departments.role: Searches, records and counterexamples for the catalogue's computable bounties
departments.brief: Work the prize problem named below. Read the source page first. Write prize_work/<id>.md (statement, prize terms, best known record, why it is hard, feasibility for a laptop) and run one bounded search or experiment yourself (script in prize_work/<id>/, at most 1 h CPU, with a gate). Report the exact range searched. Never submit anything to a sponsor.

departments.name: Packing Shop
departments.role: Solver for packing n unit squares (n = 1..1000) into the smallest square; tracks the score
departments.brief: Packing Shop (Kaggle Squares in Squares, $50k; $5k milestone prizes to the leaderboard leader on 17 Jan 2027 and 18 Apr 2027; final 18 Jul 2027). The harness is ready in prize_work/squares-in-squares/: sis.py (strict validator, score), nightly.py (runs every strategy in strategies/ for all n every night and keeps the best valid packing per n), best_score.json, submission.csv. Your job: add or improve ONE strategy file strategies/<name>.py (NAME + pack(n, seconds) -> list of (x, y, angle) or None), aimed at the n with the largest excess L/sqrt(n) - 1 (n just above a perfect square). Known families to implement and check: Goebel-style 45-degree strips, Friedman's best-known small packings (n <= 100), local optimisation (shrink + resolve overlaps). Test with `python nightly.py --minutes 2 --only <ns>` and report which n improved and the new total score. Never upload to Kaggle; Juwen submits.

departments.name: Library
departments.problem: Navier-Stokes, Yang-Mills, P vs NP, Hodge
departments.role: Reads the week's new papers on the four problems the lab does not compute on
departments.brief: Read the newest digest in automation/digests/ and pick the 3 most substantial new papers on Navier-Stokes, Yang-Mills, P vs NP or Hodge. For each write a 6-10 line brief in scout_notes/<date>.md: claim, method, status (preprint / peer reviewed / known to have gaps), and whether anything is checkable by computation here. Flag crank or unrefereed 'proofs' as such.

departments.name: Referee
departments.role: Re-runs the gates of finished jobs, downgrades overclaims
departments.brief: Review the finished lab jobs listed below. For each: re-run its script/gate, check the numbers in the result match the files, check the wording claims nothing beyond the evidence (no 'proof', no 'solved'). Write review_notes/<job id>.md (pass / fix / fail + one line), set the reviewed job's 'reviewed' field to pass|fix|fail, and fix wording in FINDINGS.md if needed.

departments.name: Press Room
departments.role: Turns reviewed results into the first-month package: BSD note, RH note, prize dossier index
departments.brief: Advance the first-month package (milestone M3): bsd_project/paper/bsd_note.md (F10/F11 + a2-weighted murmurations, honest limits, reproducible scripts listed), rh_project/paper/rh_note.md (finite-height BBLM corrections), prize_work/INDEX.md (one line per dossier). Only reviewed results go in. Drafts only: never email or publish. Also draft public posts for Juwen to publish himself (Kaggle discussion write-ups, erdosproblems.com forum comments) in outbox/public/<date>-<topic>.md, only for results the Review Panel passed. Never post.

departments.name: Review Panel
departments.problem: Simulated expert review before any real expert sees a result
departments.role: Critiques each finished result through 3 expert lenses built from published papers (labelled simulated)
departments.brief: Review Panel: before a lab result is shown to any real person, review it through three expert lenses. Build each lens ONLY from published work: pick the 3 researchers whose papers are closest to the result (automation/experts.json and the arXiv/MathSciNet record), read the relevant papers, and write what an expert grounded in THAT work would object to - methods, known counterexamples, prior results that already cover it, numerical pitfalls - each objection with a citation. Label the file clearly: 'SIMULATED review built from published papers; not the opinion of the named researchers.' Never quote or attribute opinions to real people, never use the panel in emails, never contact anyone. Re-run the result's gate script if there is one. Verdict per result: pass / fix (list) / reject. Write review_panel/<job id>.md and put the verdict in your result file as panel_verdict.

departments.name: Workshop
departments.problem: Lab tooling: Lean 4 + Mathlib, solver speed-ups
departments.role: Installs and maintains tools the other departments need (one task at a time)
departments.task: install Lean 4 (elan) + a Mathlib project so Erdos claims can be machine-checked
departments.brief: Workshop: make the lab's tools work. First task: install elan/Lean 4 without admin rights (official elan-init for Windows), create prize_work/lean/ as a Lake project depending on Mathlib, download the Mathlib cache (lake exe cache get) and check that `lake build` compiles a one-line test theorem. Record exact commands and versions in prize_work/lean/README.md. Next tasks when Lean works: speed up prize_work/squares-in-squares/sis.py (numpy or numba) without changing what it accepts.
